agents.name: Storyline Architect
agents.verdict: R1 is the cleanest story because it has a public scene, visible Aachu pressure, one private signal, Zuv action, and a funny tender payoff.
agents.keep: The one-look exit code and the 'aur batao?' receipt.
agents.cut: Any version where Zuv rescues her like a helpless person.

agents.name: Contrarian Critic
agents.verdict: R1 passes only if it avoids social-anxiety heaviness and avoids making family or guests look bad.
agents.risk: Could become 'husband saves wife from people' if staged too heroically.
agents.repair: Make the exit playful and mutual: he offers ice cream or a practical excuse, not rescue language.

agents.name: Retention Analyst
agents.verdict: R1 has the strongest two-slide open loop: she did not say it, her face did.
agents.hook_strength: A partner can immediately tag the person with an exit face.
agents.middle_reengagement: The eyebrow SOS and 'aur batao?' line create recognizable comedy.

agents.name: Visual Director
agents.verdict: R1 is the most drawable as a staged short scene: crowd edge, cup/dupatta, eyebrow, keys/door, ice cream/outside.
agents.generation_notes: Keep crowd suggested, not detailed. Use warm social interior and clean negative space; avoid wedding-glam tableau.

agents.name: Copy Chief
agents.verdict: R1 copy can stay short, spoken, and name-free.
agents.copy_warning: Do not over-explain social battery. Let the face and body language carry it.

agents.name: Algorithm / Brand Strategist
agents.verdict: R1 has the strongest partner-tag behavior because every couple has a small-talk escape code.
agents.send_save_reason: It gives language to an everyday private signal without becoming advice.

agents.name: Harsh Final Selector
agents.verdict: Select R1. R7 is the serious backup, but R1 has better comedy, clearer staging, and stronger comment behavior.

avoided_patterns: generic couple standing in a crowd
long caption text carrying the scene
food as premise instead of exit device
